It does not add\n`POST /route/task`, a second score function, or a second routing decision store.\nThe existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` meaning remains observable and\nunchanged; assignment and provenance are additive fields.\n\n## D2 — Preserve compatibility with an optional strict profile\n\nLegacy `task_signals` remains accepted with its current permissive extra-field\nbehavior because existing phase callers send fields such as `write_allow`. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nThe registry and catalog snapshots are each loaded once per request. A registry read or\nshape failure fails closed as `routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to\ncatalog-only scoring. Catalog rows with no exact configured lane projection are retained\nin `excluded` as `catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. No raw\nsecret, environment value, prompt, free-form task-signal extra, or unbounded path list\nenters either record; only typed/bounded categories and rationale enter persistence.\n\n## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest\n\nA skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It\nloads the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, and archetype model map,\nthen combines the caller's already-resolved static provider/model with the fallback\ndimension order. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy\nassociation.\n\nThe response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,\n`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded\nfailure reason. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. The reusable helper lives in\n`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from\nan explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy\ndegradation paths.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. It does not define per-mode overrides, the isolation precedence ladder, or\nenforcement; DG-05 owns that contract. It does not call routing before `dispatch_fn`,\nchange `phase_agent.py`, redispatch work, or add loop caps; DG-06 owns obedience.\nNo sandbox is launched; DG-07 owns enforcement.\n\n## D10 — Test-first packages and validation\n\nContract/config tests fail first, followed by pure policy/association tests, then service\nand transport/fallback tests. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. No raw\nsecret, environment value, prompt, free-form task-signal extra, or unbounded path list\nenters either record; only typed/bounded categories and rationale enter persistence.\n\n## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest\n\nA skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It\nloads the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, and archetype model map,\nthen combines the caller's already-resolved static provider/model with the fallback\ndimension order. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy\nassociation.\n\nThe response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,\n`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded\nfailure reason. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. The reusable helper lives in\n`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from\nan explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy\ndegradation paths.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. Extend routing to vendor × location × isolation × dispatch mode\n\n> Parent roadmap: `dispatch-governance`\n> Roadmap item: `dg-04`\n> Change ID: `implement-the-task-router-vendor-x-location-x-model`\n> Stacked on: `add-live-vendor-capability-and-cost-registry` (`dg-01`)\n\n## Summary\n\nExtend the existing adaptive model router at `POST /routing/select_model` and its\n`select_model_for_task` MCP mirror. The request gains a typed task-routing profile and\nthe selected candidate gains an exact configured lane assignment: `agent_id`, vendor\ntype, location, isolation, and dispatch mode. The dg-01 `VendorRegistryService` supplies\nlive lane feasibility and exact catalog-model projections before the dg-00 utility\nscorer ranks candidates.\n\nRouting rules are deterministic, validated, and versioned in\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml`. Coordinator decisions retain additive assignment and\npolicy provenance in both `routing_decisions` and the durable audit log. A local\nconfiguration-derived fallback returns the same assignment shape with explicit\n`fallback=true` provenance when the coordinator is unreachable.\n\nThis change does **not** create `POST /route/task`, score a second time, alter dispatch\nexecution, pin isolation precedence, or enforce a sandbox. additive routing surface\n\nThe coordinator SHALL extend `POST /routing/select_model` and its\n`select_model_for_task` MCP mirror with task-profile and assignment fields, and SHALL NOT\nadd a second task-routing endpoint or scoring path.\n\n#### Scenario: Existing HTTP and MCP surfaces stay aligned\n\n- **WHEN** the same valid task-routing request is submitted through HTTP and direct MCP\n- **THEN** both surfaces SHALL validate the same typed profile and return the same\n  assignment/provenance shape\n- **AND** no `POST /route/task` route SHALL be registered.\n\n#### Scenario: Legacy caller remains compatible\n\n- **WHEN** a caller sends only the dg-00 `task_signals.archetype` field\n- **THEN** the request SHALL remain valid\n- **AND** newly added input and output fields SHALL use additive defaults.\n\n### Requirement: Typed task-routing profile\n\nThe request SHALL type phase/archetype, expected duration, scope, interactivity, secret\nneed, parallelism, repository shape, roadmap policy, and optional location, isolation,\nand dispatch-mode constraints at the HTTP/MCP boundary.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid profile is rejected at the boundary\n\n- **WHEN** a task profile contains an invalid enum, negative duration, non-positive\n  parallelism, or malformed policy constraint\n- **THEN** HTTP SHALL return 422\n- **AND** direct MCP SHALL return the existing matching validation-error envelope.\n\n#### Scenario: Config rules consume typed signals\n\n- **WHEN** a validated `routing.yaml` rule matches a task-profile field\n- **THEN** its configured location, isolation, or dispatch-mode constraint SHALL be\n  applied deterministically\n- **AND** the matching rule ID SHALL be recorded in decision provenance.\n\n### Requirement: Registry-backed feasibility precedes utility\n\nThe router SHALL consume `VendorRegistryService` in process and remove infeasible\nlane/model assignments before invoking the existing dg-00 utility scorer.\n\n#### Scenario: Exact lane and catalog association\n\n- **WHEN** a registry lane projects a catalog model\n- **THEN** routing SHALL associate it only by the exact projected catalog vendor, model,\n  endpoint-kind, and base-URL identity\n- **AND** SHALL NOT infer association from agent ID suffixes, publisher names, or fuzzy\n  model strings.\n\n#### Scenario: Infeasible assignment cannot win\n\n- **WHEN** a lane is unavailable, rate limited, lacks the archetype or dispatch mode, or\n  violates location, isolation, or roadmap-policy constraints\n- **THEN** the lane/model assignment SHALL be excluded before dg-00 utility scoring\n- **AND** the exclusion SHALL carry a machine-readable reason.\n\n#### Scenario: Registry failure fails closed\n\n- **WHEN** the in-process registry snapshot cannot be loaded or validated\n- **THEN** routing SHALL fail with `routing-registry-unavailable`\n- **AND** SHALL NOT score catalog-only candidates or infer a lane association.\n\n#### Scenario: Unprojected catalog candidate remains explainable\n\n- **WHEN** a catalog row has no exact configured lane projection\n- **THEN** it SHALL NOT enter utility scoring\n- **AND** it SHALL appear in exclusions as `catalog:no-configured-lane`.\n\n#### Scenario: Feasible assignments retain dg-00 ranking\n\n- **WHEN** two or more lane/model assignments remain feasible\n- **THEN** their quality, cost, latency, headroom, and exploration ranking SHALL be\n  produced by the existing dg-00 scorer without a second utility function\n- **AND** equal scores SHALL be ordered by agent ID and exact catalog identity.\n\n### Requirement: Versioned deterministic routing policy\n\nRouting dimension rules SHALL be loaded from a schema-validated `routing.yaml` carrying\nan explicit schema version and policy version.\n\n#### Scenario: Policy edit changes a decision\n\n- **WHEN** a test changes a valid constraint rule or dispatch default in `routing.yaml`\n- **THEN** the resulting assignment SHALL change without a Python code edit\n- **AND** repeated evaluation of the same profile, registry snapshot, catalog snapshot,\n  and policy SHALL produce the same ordered candidates when exploration is disabled.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid policy fails loud\n\n- **WHEN** `routing.yaml` contains an unknown field, unsupported schema version, invalid\n  enum, duplicate rule ID, or reference to an unconfigured phase dispatch default\n- **THEN** policy loading SHALL fail before routing a task\n- **AND** SHALL NOT silently substitute permissive defaults.\n\n### Requirement: Additive assignment and provenance\n\nEvery selected candidate SHALL expose exact lane assignment fields and every persisted\ndecision SHALL retain the task profile, policy version/checksum, matched rules, excluded\nassignments, and source.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator decision is durable and auditable\n\n- **WHEN** the coordinator returns a routing decision\n- **THEN** the same decision ID and assignment SHALL be written to `routing_decisions`\n- **AND** a link-only coordinator audit event SHALL record decision ID, selected\n  agent/model, routing-policy version/checksum, source, and success\n- **AND** both records SHALL commit atomically before the response is returned.\n\n#### Scenario: Durable write cannot be established\n\n- **WHEN** the atomic decision-and-audit RPC fails\n- **THEN** neither record SHALL remain committed\n- **AND** HTTP SHALL return 503 detail `routing-durability-unavailable`\n- **AND** MCP SHALL return its existing matching 503 error envelope.\n\n#### Scenario: Persistence projection is bounded\n\n- **WHEN** permissive legacy task signals include undeclared values such as path lists\n- **THEN** the request remains valid for compatibility\n- **AND** persistence SHALL retain only declared task signals and the typed routing\n  profile, excluding all legacy extras.\n\n#### Scenario: Alternative candidates retain lane identity\n\n- **WHEN** feasible alternatives are returned\n- **THEN** each alternative SHALL retain its own exact `agent_id`, vendor type,\n  location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base URL.\n\n### Requirement: Honest local fallback\n\nA coordinator-unreachable client path SHALL derive a deterministic assignment only from\nthe checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, archetype model map, and caller's\nstatic model/provider inputs.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator is unreachable\n\n- **WHEN** the coordinator routing operation times out or is unreachable\n- **THEN** the local helper SHALL return the normal assignment shape with\n  `fallback=true`, `source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, and\n  `durable_audit=false`\n- **AND** SHALL NOT embed a roster, synthesize live availability, or claim a coordinator\n  audit record exists\n- **AND** its catalog key SHALL be null because no live catalog join occurred.\n\n#### Scenario: Existing static fallback equality is preserved\n\n- **WHEN** existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` adaptive routing is disabled, fails,\n  returns malformed data, or exceeds its bounded timeout\n- **THEN** the returned `ResolvedArchetype` SHALL equal the dg-00 static result exactly.\n"}]},"isError":false}

Success after ~a month: (a) autopilot/quick-task runs complete with\nno manual model picks, (b) local models absorb a meaningful share of economy-tier traffic.\n\n## What Changes\n\n### dg-00 recovery boundary (2026-09-16)\n\nThe current roadmap item and PR deliver the four dg-00 wiring outcomes: five HTTP paths plus the\nMCP selection tool; additive catalog storage with storage-only reads; default-off adaptive\ndelegation with exact static fallback; and dispatcher discovery for `OpenAICompatAdapter`. The\nsupporting tranche also schedules the implemented catalog refresher, local health probe, and\nledger rollup independently. The remaining original vision is preserved in `deferred-tasks.md`\nand `deferred-specs/`; this tranche does not migrate central model ownership from PR 417 and\ndoes not add ri-18 billing metadata to `CandidateInput`.\n\n### Full proposal vision (preserved, deferred outside dg-00)\n\nThe bullets below record the original vision. They are not delivery claims for this PR except\nwhere the bounded paragraph above names an implemented substrate component.\n\n- **New capability `model-routing`** owning the model catalog, scoring, and selection contract.\n- **Model catalog + signal ledger in coordinator Postgres** (new migrations): per\n  `(vendor, model, endpoint_kind, archetype/task-type)` rows carrying benchmark priors\n  (Artificial Analysis scores, rankings), per-Mtok pricing, observed latency, and feedback\n  posteriors. Absorbs the arbitrage instrument's five parts: signal schema + decision provenance,\n  metered-counterfactual cost ledger, active probes (ToS-diff monitor, model canary), Cedar hard\n  constraints (e.g. Claude subscription = programmatic-ineligible), and tripwires (vendor freeze,\n  economic kill, prior invalidation on canary drift).\n- **OpenRouter catalog refresher**: scheduled job (coordinator `WatchdogService`) pulling\n  `models-list` / `model-endpoints` / `benchmarks` / `rankings-daily` via a standing OpenRouter\n  API key (not the 7-day OAuth MCP key); local endpoints register into the same catalog via\n  health probe.\n- **`select_model_for_task` resolver** in `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py`, exposed as\n  HTTP `POST /routing/select_model` and MCP tool alongside `resolve_for_phase`. Score =\n  benchmark prior + task-type posterior − λ_cost·cost-per-completed-task − λ_latency·latency\n  (per-Mtok price is only the cost prior for unsampled pairs; see design D3), with **configurable\n  objective weights** (cost/quality/resilience profile) and an **explicit exploration budget knob**\n  (percent-of-tasks and monthly-$ ceiling, policy-enforced).\n- **OpenAI-compatible `base_url` dispatch adapter** in\n  `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py` covering OpenRouter (metered,\n  under a **monthly spend ceiling**) and local Ollama/vLLM endpoints from day one.\n- **Replace the cost stub**: `policy.py::_estimate_cost_delta` and `evaluate_policy` read real\n  catalog pricing; `generation-get` reconciles actual OpenRouter spend.\n- **Feedback aggregator** rolling `vendor_notes`, `VendorSwitch` deltas, gen-eval scores, and\n  `memory_procedural` counts into per-(model, task-type) posteriors (decayed averages first).\n- **Optional proactive quota probe** (design D13): a worker-side adapter over the read-only\n  `quota-axi` CLI surfacing per-provider remaining-window headroom into catalog feasibility and\n  the resilience objective; `agents.yaml` gains `endpoint_kind`/`base_url`\n  fields. *Rollback plan*: feature flag `ROUTING_ADAPTIVE=off` reverts to static archetype tier\n  resolution (existing behavior preserved as the fallback path); The latent-intent check confirmed the scope/coordinator-dependency\ntrade-off is acceptable in exchange for fleet-wide learning and automation. Approaches B and C\nbelow are retained as brief records of the rejected directions.\n\n### Approach A — Coordinator-native selection service (full absorption) — **Recommended**\n\nCatalog, ledger, posteriors, and the resolver live in the coordinator (Postgres + FastAPI/MCP);\nskills stay the dispatch/execution layer; dashboard reads coordinator API.\n\n- **Pros**: single fleet-wide source of truth (calibration requires cross-machine aggregation —\n  both absorbed proposals independently reached the same conclusion); works for cloud (HTTP) and\n  local (MCP) agents; matches the layered architecture (decision = Coordination, hard constraints\n  = Governance/Cedar, dispatch = Execution); one coherent home for the absorbed schemas.\n- **Cons**: largest scope — needs migrations, watchdog jobs, API surface; coordinator becomes a\n  routing dependency (mitigated: resolver failure falls back to static tiers).\n- **Effort**: L (decomposed into parallel work packages below).\n\n### Approach B — Skills-layer router with file-based state\n\nExtend `policy.py`/`parallel-infrastructure` directly; catalog and posteriors as versioned\nYAML/JSON in the repo or roadmap workspace; OpenRouter queried at dispatch time.\n\n- **Pros**: no coordinator changes; incremental; works with coordinator down.\n- **Cons**: per-machine state defeats fleet calibration (the learning goal); racy under parallel\n  agents; contradicts the absorbed instrument's placement decision (audit_log + OTel); dispatch-time\n  OpenRouter calls add latency and a network dependency to every routing decision.\n- **Effort**: M.\n\n### Approach C — External gateway (LiteLLM-style proxy) as the router\n\nPoint all SDK dispatch at a self-hosted LiteLLM (or OpenRouter directly); routing, fallbacks, and\nbudgets configured in the gateway; coordinator only records outcomes.\n\n- **Pros**: battle-tested routing/budget/fallback machinery for free; `base_url` unification comes\n  built-in; least custom code.\n- **Cons**: cannot route CLI-subscription dispatch (Claude Code/Codex/Gemini CLIs — the majority\n  of traffic and the entire arbitrage edge live outside any HTTP proxy); gateway config cannot\n  consume task-specific feedback posteriors; new always-on infrastructure to operate; subscription\n  EULA constraints can't be expressed as gateway config.\n- **Effort**: M–L.\n\n**Recommendation rationale**: A is the only approach that serves the stated latent intent\n(fleet-wide learning + automation). B sacrifices the learning asset to per-machine state; C cannot\nsee the subscription-CLI traffic that dominates both volume and savings. (`skills/autopilot-roadmap/scripts/policy.py::_estimate_cost_delta`), so every\nrun either overpays a premium model for easy work or requires the operator to hand-pick vendors —\nand nothing the fleet learns about model×task performance is retained. The OpenRouter MCP server\n(live `models-list`, `benchmarks`, `rankings-daily`, `model-endpoints` pricing/latency) plus the\nfeedback plumbing this repo already defines but never populates (`LearningEntry.vendor_notes`,\n`VendorSwitch` expected-vs-observed deltas, `memory_procedural` counters, gen-eval scores) make an\nadaptive router buildable now: benchmark-calibrated priors, task-feedback posteriors, and\nconfigurable cost/quality/resilience trade-offs, covering subscription CLIs, metered APIs\n(including OpenRouter itself), and local endpoints (Ollama/vLLM).\n\n**Latent intent (from discovery)**: automation of the model-choice decision and durable learning\nabout model×task fit are the primary goals; cost cutting and resilience are configurable\nobjectives, not fixed ones. Success after ~a month: (a) autopilot/quick-task runs complete with\nno manual model picks, (b) local models absorb a meaningful share of economy-tier traffic.\n\n## What Changes\n\n### dg-00 recovery boundary (2026-09-16)\n\nThe current roadmap item and PR deliver the four dg-00 wiring outcomes: five HTTP paths plus the\nMCP selection tool; additive catalog storage with storage-only reads; default-off adaptive\ndelegation with exact static fallback; and dispatcher discovery for `OpenAICompatAdapter`. The\nsupporting tranche also schedules the implemented catalog refresher, local health probe, and\nledger rollup independently. The remaining original vision is preserved in `deferred-tasks.md`\nand `deferred-specs/`; this tranche does not migrate central model ownership from PR 417 and\ndoes not add ri-18 billing metadata to `CandidateInput`.\n\n### Full proposal vision (preserved, deferred outside dg-00)\n\nThe bullets below record the original vision. Absorbs the arbitrage instrument's five parts: signal schema + decision provenance,\n  metered-counterfactual cost ledger, active probes (ToS-diff monitor, model canary), Cedar hard\n  constraints (e.g. Claude subscription = programmatic-ineligible), and tripwires (vendor freeze,\n  economic kill, prior invalidation on canary drift).\n- **OpenRouter catalog refresher**: scheduled job (coordinator `WatchdogService`) pulling\n  `models-list` / `model-endpoints` / `benchmarks` / `rankings-daily` via a standing OpenRouter\n  API key (not the 7-day OAuth MCP key); local endpoints register into the same catalog via\n  health probe.\n- **`select_model_for_task` resolver** in `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py`, exposed as\n  HTTP `POST /routing/select_model` and MCP tool alongside `resolve_for_phase`. Score =\n  benchmark prior + task-type posterior − λ_cost·cost-per-completed-task − λ_latency·latency\n  (per-Mtok price is only the cost prior for unsampled pairs; see design D3), with **configurable\n  objective weights** (cost/quality/resilience profile) and an **explicit exploration budget knob**\n  (percent-of-tasks and monthly-$ ceiling, policy-enforced).\n- **OpenAI-compatible `base_url` dispatch adapter** in\n  `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py` covering OpenRouter (metered,\n  under a **monthly spend ceiling**) and local Ollama/vLLM endpoints from day one.\n- **Replace the cost stub**: `policy.py::_estimate_cost_delta` and `evaluate_policy` read real\n  catalog pricing; `generation-get` reconciles actual OpenRouter spend.\n- **Feedback aggregator** rolling `vendor_notes`, `VendorSwitch` deltas, gen-eval scores, and\n  `memory_procedural` counts into per-(model, task-type) posteriors (decayed averages first).\n- **Optional proactive quota probe** (design D13): a worker-side adapter over the read-only\n  `quota-axi` CLI surfacing per-provider remaining-window headroom into catalog feasibility and\n  the resilience objective; migrations are additive-only.\n- **Full proposal (deferred): archive the two absorbed draft changes** with pointers to this change.\n\n## Approaches Considered\n\n### Selected Approach\n\n**Approach A — coordinator-native selection service** (selected at Gate 1, 2026-07-08, no\nmodifications requested). The latent-intent check confirmed the scope/coordinator-dependency\ntrade-off is acceptable in exchange for fleet-wide learning and automation. Approaches B and C\nbelow are retained as brief records of the rejected directions.\n\n### Approach A — Coordinator-native selection service (full absorption) — **Recommended**\n\nCatalog, ledger, posteriors, and the resolver live in the coordinator (Postgres + FastAPI/MCP);\nskills stay the dispatch/execution layer; dashboard reads coordinator API.\n\n- **Pros**: single fleet-wide source of truth (calibration requires cross-machine aggregation —\n  both absorbed proposals independently reached the same conclusion); works for cloud (HTTP) and\n  local (MCP) agents; matches the layered architecture (decision = Coordination, hard constraints\n  = Governance/Cedar, dispatch = Execution); one coherent home for the absorbed schemas.\n- **Cons**: largest scope — needs migrations, watchdog jobs, API surface; coordinator becomes a\n  routing dependency (mitigated: resolver failure falls back to static tiers).\n- **Effort**: L (decomposed into parallel work packages below).\n\n### Approach B — Skills-layer router with file-based state\n\nExtend `policy.py`/`parallel-infrastructure` directly; catalog and posteriors as versioned\nYAML/JSON in the repo or roadmap workspace; OpenRouter queried at dispatch time.\n\n- **Pros**: no coordinator changes; incremental; works with coordinator down.\n- **Cons**: per-machine state defeats fleet calibration (the learning goal); racy under parallel\n  agents; contradicts the absorbed instrument's placement decision (audit_log + OTel); dispatch-time\n  OpenRouter calls add latency and a network dependency to every routing decision.\n- **Effort**: M.\n\n### Approach C — External gateway (LiteLLM-style proxy) as the router\n\nPoint all SDK dispatch at a self-hosted LiteLLM (or OpenRouter directly); routing, fallbacks, and\nbudgets configured in the gateway; coordinator only records outcomes.\n\n- **Pros**: battle-tested routing/budget/fallback machinery for free; `base_url` unification comes\n  built-in; least custom code.\n- **Cons**: cannot route CLI-subscription dispatch (Claude Code/Codex/Gemini CLIs — the majority\n  of traffic and the entire arbitrage edge live outside any HTTP proxy); gateway config cannot\n  consume task-specific feedback posteriors; new always-on infrastructure to operate; subscription\n  EULA constraints can't be expressed as gateway config.\n- **Effort**: M–L.\n\n**Recommendation rationale**: A is the only approach that serves the stated latent intent\n(fleet-wide learning + automation). B sacrifices the learning asset to per-machine state; C cannot\nsee the subscription-CLI traffic that dominates both volume and savings. A's main con (scope) is\nmanageable because the static-tier path remains the fallback and all schema work was already\ndesigned in the absorbed proposals.\n\n## Impact\n\n### Canonical dg-00 impact\n\n| Capability (spec delta) | Nature |\n|---|---|\n| `model-routing` (**new**) | Catalog storage/refresher, local endpoint registry/probes, resolver transport, usage ledger, and bounded static fallback |\n| `agent-coordinator` | Five routing HTTP paths plus MCP selection parity, migration 040, and three independent watchdog jobs |\n| `agent-archetypes` | Default-off adaptive delegation and endpoint metadata |\n| `parallel-infrastructure` | OpenAI-compatible reviewer discovery after CLI and SDK adapters |\n\n**Code**: `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py`, `src/coordination_api.py`,\n`src/coordination_mcp.py`, `src/http_proxy.py`, new `src/model_routing/`,\n`database/migrations/040_model_routing.sql`,\n`skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py`, and focused tests.\n\nThe catalog pricing and scoring core referenced by dg-00 already exists on `main` from PR #237;\nthis change wires it into storage and transports rather than creating a second implementation.\n\n### Full-proposal impact (preserved and deferred)\n\nThe following table and code list describe the original full proposal. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nThe registry and catalog snapshots are each loaded once per request. Catalog rows with no exact configured lane projection are retained\nin `excluded` as `catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance.
